beta_new: Pull the same overhang as the neighbouring route Second Thoughts, then keep going directly upward past one bolt to a pine used as the anchor.

The first pitch holds the crux, jamming the obvious overhanging crack up to a belay equipped with bolts. You can lower off there or carry on to an offset crack on pitch 2, and then swing over a roof on pitch 3 before easy ground to the summit.
Unbroken crack climbing on the lean-over northern corner of this tower. Link past the first possible hanging stance. The way down is a rappel east followed by the east ledges.

moves.from: a rack of nuts handles it

beta_new: The traverse: from South Arapaho's summit, follow the connecting ridge north, about three quarters of a mile one way. Almost all of it is Class 3, with roughly 300 ft of downclimbing and 400 ft of climbing each way, including a somewhat exposed Class 3 downclimb of about 50 ft early on. Stay near the crest and escape to the west side at difficulties; the east side drops to the glacier. Occasional painted marks and cairns show the line but are sparse. The crux: about three quarters of the way to North Arapaho, two short steps of roughly 8-10 ft each go at Class 4 on good holds; some parties find a line that stays Class 3. Final slopes: easier ground, sometimes with a lingering snow patch, leads to North Arapaho's broad summit. Allow at least an hour each way on the ridge.

moves.from: Trail to South Arapaho: follow the Arapaho Pass trail to the Fourth of July Mine ruins, then switch back northeast on the signed Arapaho Glacier trail. It climbs steadily above treeline to the saddle southeast of South Arapaho, where the trail ends and a rocky, loose Class 2 scramble past a false summit leads to the top.
moves.value: The scramble from the saddle to South Arapaho's summit is rocky and loose Class 2, passing a false summit.

beta_new: Start exactly as for the neighbouring route Jester: four bolts take you across the roof, then onto the face above.

The start ledge is reached by a delicate downclimb. Face climb to gain the thin cracks, stemming the corner, then jam the strenuous finger-width crack as it trends rightward, finishing on gravelly easier rock.

moves.from: Bring thin gear for the crack.

beta_new: A steep slab with a trio of fixed bolts plus a dike to use, ending at chained anchors.

moves.from: carry a few nuts as extra insurance

value.text: A few nuts as extra insurance.

beta_new: Share the opening with the neighbouring route The Destroyer, then roughly 30 feet up traverse across to the southern side and tackle a severely steep wall, clipping four bolts.
Four bolts lead up a sheer wall facing west just right of a sloping arete; use the crack along one side of the flake, then pull hard to continue upward.
A striking prow, found past a dead tree: a slim corner gives access to an arete with three bolts.

moves.from: Small cams are handy for the lower crack.

value.text: Small cams for the lower crack.

beta_new: Follow a slender corner that faces right and has two bolts to clip along the way.

Start in the gap separating the freestanding block from the cliff. Reaching the first of four bolts is the crux, so use a stick-clip if possible; above, pockets and edges make for pleasant face climbing.

Follows a dark streak of water stain on the wall's southern side. Powerful pocket pulls over the opening 30 feet lead to a rest, then strenuous moves up a faint crack get you over a small overhang to the anchors.
Begin where the trees cast shade, climb leftward past two bolts, and merge with the neighbouring route Between Nothingness and Eternity. The climbing above is easier.
Squeeze up the deep chimney separating Bonzo from Kor's Flake, which marks the western edge of the buttress; this chimney is also the rappel-in point for a neighbouring route.
The opening moves are the crux and are difficult to protect.

moves.from: so pack wires, TCUs and some mid-size cams

value.text: Wires, TCUs and some mid-size cams.

moves.from: Descend by the rappel route used for the neighbouring route Don Juan.

beta_new: Follow a corner toward the wall's left-hand end, then finish with a hand traverse rightward at the top, clipping five bolts along the way.

This traversing line starts up Carpenter's Corner, then crosses the whole rock to join the last pitch of Hand Jive over six pitches, with a downclimb near the foot of a neighbouring dihedral along the way.
Scramble up to a pedestal, then follow the spotless buttress overhead, clipping five bolts to reach cold-shut anchors. Do not fumble the opening clips, or a fall would land you on the pedestal.

A groove with no protection leads to a slim, tapering overhang; stride over it to finish at anchors. The first pitch begins right of the neighbouring route Jazzman and follows a corner onto the adjacent slab.
Trend rightward on very thin edges and precarious smears, clipping five bolts, up to an easy but runout slab. Belay off boulders sitting on the ramp higher up.

An aid line from the past, reached by climbing the lower two pitches of a neighbouring route. A groove then leads to a boulder-strewn ledge; climb the corner above, mantel up onto a finger-width crack where the corner swings left, then follow a much tighter crack to two old bolts (back them up).

Edge straight up from the trees to a bolt, then work left into the water groove covered in crystals, climb it, and drift leftward onto a seam that accepts big nuts and small cams. Pay out the rope all the way to the ramp where you belay.
Follow the large, lichen-covered dihedral that faces right; an old bolt sits roughly 60 feet up. Higher up it merges with the neighbouring Bitty Buttress route.
Squeeze up the chimney that sits at the very back of the approach gully; it finishes at the foot of West Chimney.
Steep face climbing alongside a crack toward a belay point. Be aware that the one existing piton is poor.

moves.from: Carry plenty of mid-size protection, such as cams and hexes

value.text: Plenty of mid-size protection, such as cams and hexes.

beta_new: Share the beginning with the neighbouring route Top Dawg, then veer leftward once you clip the first bolt, climbing a steep face of sidepulls and layback moves. Finish on the slab above, clipping the other route's anchors.

moves.from: Small RPs fit between bolts two and three; wired nuts help up high.

beta_new: Follow the seam-crack as it angles right. The crux comes right off the ground, with thin laybacks and pinching undercling holds. Bring small wired nuts and RPs low and cams higher; the descent is a rappel from a two-bolt anchor on top of the corner.

Enter from the left side (a dicey 5.9 section), then jam up the strenuous dihedral to a belay on two bolts. A one-rope rappel leads left into the chimney of Banana Peels; better still, keep going on Chain of Command.
Chimney up the black slot a little right of another line. Use the anchors belonging to the neighbouring Cracking Up.

Climb about 20 feet on either neighbouring line, then follow the slender crack running between them, which widens to a flared flake near the finish. Lower from the anchor belonging to the adjacent route.
Start near Winds of Fortune and pull the roof using a square jug, then run up the face, bear left past a bulge, then end with a fist-width crack.

moves.from: Rappel eastward from a tree afterwards.

beta_new: Follows roughly the same line as the neighbouring Hot Licks and shares its belays. Wedge up the widening flared crack beside it and veer rightward at a bolt, face climb past three more bolts with a hard move at the final one, then climb a steep dihedral that faces right to finish.
Protection is mostly fixed.

moves.from: carry long runners to thread through the pockets; large nuts are an optional addition

value.text: Long runners to thread through the pockets, and optionally large nuts.

beta_new: Start atop a boulder beneath the face. Move up and leftward to a small overhang, undercling rightward under it and lean back to a rest beneath a shallow corner. The corner holds the crux, then edge across leftward to a finger-width seam.

moves.from: the upper seam wants TCUs plus small cams

value.text: TCUs and small cams for the upper seam.

beta_new: Crawl through the boulder tunnel to the dihedral and jam its crack, then make a tough exit at the crescent roof, leftward, to a bolted stance. Pitch two frictions up a bolted slab. A direct start edges rightward from the boulders past a line of bolts.

moves.from: Bring gear to 3 inches for the crack.

value.text: Gear to 3 in for the crack.

beta_new: Work upward to the dark water-streaked groove, then edge up and to the right to reach the broad ledge below the roofs. The final bolt is awkwardly placed, so plan the clip.
Climb the slab past one bolt, then angle leftward past a second bolt to reach the belay and rappel anchors shared with the neighbouring groove route.
The lower section is broken, but the dihedral up high holds a smooth, pleasant hand crack. Protect it with cams up to about #3.

Pick through the bushes to the dihedral's base, jam up past a bulge and undercling around a big flake, placing small RPs. Belay on a stance with slings, or stretch the rope to a ledge behind a block. Pitch two can merge into a neighbouring crack or follow an easy groove.
